sections.h2: Which office files deeds for Surry County land?
sections.html:
The Register of Deeds in Dobson. The office is at 201 East Kapp Street, with P.O. Box 303 for mail, and answers at (336) 401-8150. Every parcel in the county is recorded in this one office.

Walk-in hours differ by task. Counter service runs from 8:15 am to 5:00 pm, except Tuesday, when doors open at 9:00 am. Real estate filings stop at 4:30 pm, half an hour before closing time, so a late-afternoon courier run can slip to the following day. Faxed real estate paperwork has its own line, (336) 401-8149, distinct from the vital records fax.

Surry County accepts it. The office takes e-recorded documents from two companies: Simplifile and Corporation Service Company.

Most title companies and closing attorneys already hold an account with one of them, so a closing can be recorded without anyone driving to Dobson. If you are selling without an attorney, ask the person handling your closing how the deed will be submitted. Simplifile's number is (800) 460-5657, and Corporation Service Company has a web address on the county's real estate page.

  • Electronic submission goes through an approved vendor, not directly through the county website.
  • Paper deeds can be delivered in person or mailed to the P.O. Box.
  • The real estate fax line is separate from the vital records fax line, so use (336) 401-8149 only for real estate matters.

sections.h2: Filing fees at the Dobson desk
sections.html:
Fees come from state law and are the same in every county. G.S. 161-10 sets the price of an ordinary instrument by page count and makes its fee list exclusive. Open the statute for the current schedule, and ask the Dobson office about any add-on for an oversized or nonstandard document.

A seller seldom writes this check, because the buyer's closing costs usually absorb recording. Your contract controls that point, so read it before closing day.

sections.h2: Who pays the excise tax when a Surry County house sells?
sections.html:
You do, as the seller. The deed stamp tax, found in G.S. 105-228.30, falls on the person transferring title and must reach the register before the deed is filed.

The amount rises with the price, so ask your closer for the exact line on the settlement statement instead of working it out yourself. Receipts are shared between the county and the State. If your acreage straddles a county line, the tax goes to the county holding the larger share of the value.

sections.h2: Why filing order protects a seller
sections.html:
Filing is what protects the buyer's title, and your clean exit with it. Under G.S. 47-18, a deed, long lease, option or right of first refusal carries no force against lien creditors or purchasers for value until it is registered, and the earlier filing wins.

So a signing is only half of a closing. Until the clerk stamps the deed into the record, someone with a claim against you could be placed ahead of your buyer. A same-day e-recording avoids the Tuesday late opening and the 4:30 pm cutoff entirely.

Once the deed is filed, request the book and page or instrument number from your title company. You or a future owner can use that reference in the online search.

sections.h2: Land records and how far back they go
sections.html:
The records start in 1771, the year Surry County was formed from Rowan County. The early collection includes deeds from agents of Lord Granville, state land grants, sheriff's deeds, mortgages and property divisions. Original books can be viewed or copied through the imaging system, and they also exist on microfilm and in book form. The oldest index covers 1771 to 1870, and a second index runs from 1870 to 1937.

Land that now sits in Stokes, Forsyth or Yadkin may appear in early Surry volumes. Online search and recording standards are linked from the real estate page.

If a title problem surfaces during a sale, a title examiner usually does this research. A seller can still look up the chain of ownership to find a missing release or an old easement.

sections.h2: Can personal information be removed from records online?
sections.html:
Yes, within limits. G.S. 132-1.10(f) allows certain personal identifiers to be redacted from the website copy of a record, and the county publishes a redaction request form.

The request must be in writing, signed by the requester or an agent with power of attorney, and must name the information and the document. Items that can be covered include Social Security numbers, driver's license and passport numbers, bank account numbers and card numbers or PINs. Only the website image changes. The official record kept in the deed vault stays as it was recorded.

This matters if you recorded an old deed that contains a number you would rather not have online. Call (336) 401-8150 before sending a request.

sections.h2: Housing context for a Surry County sale
sections.html:
The typical owner-occupied home is valued at $177,600, and owners live in 73.4% of homes. Median gross rent is $761 and median household income is $55,656. The county had 34,405 housing units in mid-2025, and builders pulled 244 permits during 2025.

Because stamp tax follows price, a sale at these values typically carries a modest tax line on the settlement statement.

sections.h2: What to bring to a Surry County closing
sections.html:
Bring identification, the signed deed, and payoff statements for any loan on the property. When a lender is paid off, its release is filed as a cancellation of the deed of trust, and state law charges nothing for that filing.

  • A deed that follows the recording standards linked on the county page.
  • Money or instructions covering the stamp tax.
  • Notarized authority if someone signs for you under a power of attorney.
  • The name of whoever will file the deed, by e-recording or over the counter.

Inherited homes add one step: ask the superior court clerk which estate papers must be on file before a buyer's attorney will accept the deed.

Plan the day around the office clock. A deed that reaches the counter after 4:30 pm will wait for the next business day, and Tuesday mornings begin at 9:00 am. If your closing is late in the day, ask the closer to e-record through Simplifile or Corporation Service Company so the filing does not depend on a courier.

The property tax bill is a separate matter. Recording a deed does not change it, so settle the current year with your closer and ask the Surry County tax office for the amount.

faqs.q: Where is the Surry County deed office?
faqs.a: It is 201 East Kapp Street, Dobson, NC 27017, with a mailing address of P.O. Box 303 and a main phone of (336) 401-8150. Real estate filings are taken until 4:30 pm on weekdays.

faqs.q: Can my closing company e-record a deed in Surry County?
faqs.a: Yes, through Simplifile or Corporation Service Company, the two vendors the office accepts. Ask your closer which one they use.

faqs.q: Which party owes the stamp tax on a Surry County sale?
faqs.a: The seller does. G.S. 105-228.30 puts the deed stamp tax on whoever transfers title, payable ahead of recording.

faqs.q: How much does the register charge to record an ordinary deed?
faqs.a: The schedule is statewide and printed in G.S. 161-10. Ask the Dobson office for the figure that fits your page count.

faqs.q: Does recording a deed change the property tax bill?
faqs.a: No. The bill follows the parcel, not the recording. Settle the current year with your closer and ask the Surry County tax office for the amount.
